definition: In this historical source, a joke is something understood or appreciated through a person’s sense of the incongruous, as part of aesthetic feeling. It is treated as an example of the capacity to recognize and respond to certain kinds of mental amusement.

reasons: The phrase about being “an example of the capacity to recognize and respond to certain kinds of mental amusement” is not supported by the source packet; the packet only links joke to the power of appreciating the incongruous in the context of aesthetic feelings.
The definition adds a broader interpretive gloss that goes beyond the historical wording in the packet.

The packet only states that “Esthetic Feelings” include “understanding a pun or joke,” along with “the incongruous” as something appreciated; it does not define a joke as “something understood or appreciated through a person’s sense of the incongruous.”

The definition claims the joke is “treated as an example of the capacity to recognize and respond to certain kinds of mental amusement,” but the packet does not mention “recognize,” “respond,” “mental amusement,” or any capacity framed this way.
